items.t: Electrolytes: check periodically. Hydrochlorothiazide can cause hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia (sometimes with neurological symptoms), hypomagnesaemia, hypercalcaemia; telmisartan can cause hyperkalaemia (risk factors: renal insufficiency, heart failure, diabetes).

items.t: Hepatic impairment or progressive liver disease: caution (electrolyte shifts may precipitate hepatic coma); no clinical experience in hepatic impairment.

src.q: telmisartan/HCTZ should be used with caution in patients with impaired hepatic function or progressive liver disease, since minor alterations of fluid and electrolyte balance may precipitate hepatic coma

items.t: Diabetes: thiazides may impair glucose tolerance, while hypoglycaemia may occur with insulin/antidiabetics; consider glucose monitoring and dose adjustment. Hyperuricaemia or gout may occur.

src.q: Thiazide therapy may impair glucose tolerance, whereas hypoglycaemia may occur in diabetic patients under insulin or antidiabetic therapy and telmisartan treatment.
Hyperuricaemia may occur or frank gout may be precipitated in some patients receiving thiazide therapy.

items.t: Non-melanoma skin cancer: risk rises with cumulative hydrochlorothiazide dose; advise skin checks and sun protection; reconsider after previous skin cancer (MHRA).

src.q: Patients taking HCTZ should be informed of the risk of NMSC and advised to regularly check their skin for any new lesions and promptly report any suspicious skin lesions.

items.t: Choroidal effusion, acute myopia, acute angle-closure glaucoma: stop hydrochlorothiazide as quickly as possible (risk factors: sulfonamide or penicillin allergy). ARDS: withdraw; do not give hydrochlorothiazide again after previous ARDS with it.

src.q: The primary treatment is to discontinue hydrochlorothiazide as rapidly as possible.
Hydrochlorothiazide should not be administered to patients who previously experienced ARDS following hydrochlorothiazide intake.

items.t: Aortic or mitral stenosis, obstructive cardiomyopathy: special caution. Primary aldosteronism: not recommended. Ischaemic heart or cerebrovascular disease: excessive blood pressure fall could cause MI or stroke. SLE may be activated; photosensitivity (stop if it occurs).

items.t: Lithium: not recommended; if essential, monitor lithium carefully.

items.t: Potassium-raising medicines (ACE inhibitors, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium salt substitutes, ciclosporin, heparin): not recommended; monitor potassium if prescribed.

src.q: concomitant use of the above medicinal products may lead to increases in serum potassium and is, therefore, not recommended

items.t: Potassium-losing medicines (other diuretics, laxatives, corticosteroids, amphotericin, salicylates): monitor potassium. Digoxin, antiarrhythmics and torsades-inducing medicines: periodic potassium and ECG monitoring.

src.q: If these substances are to be prescribed with the HCTZ-telmisartan combination, monitoring of potassium plasma levels is advised.

items.t: NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors and anti-inflammatory-dose aspirin): reduced diuretic and antihypertensive effects; possible acute renal failure in compromised renal function. Use with caution; hydrate; consider renal monitoring.

src.q: may reduce the diuretic, natriuretic and antihypertensive effects of thiazide diuretics and the antihypertensive effects of angiotensin II receptor blockers
Therefore the combination should be administered with caution, especially in the elderly.

items.t: Antidiabetics: dose adjustment may be needed. Metformin: use with precaution (lactic acidosis). Calcium or vitamin D: monitor calcium. Allopurinol: more hypersensitivity reactions. Beta-blockers: enhanced hyperglycaemia. Methotrexate: increased myelosuppression.

src.q: Dose adjustment of the antidiabetic medicinal products may be required

serum calcium levels should be monitored and calcium dose adjusted accordingly

src.q: Taking an ARB in early pregnancy is unlikely to harm your baby.
an ARB should usually be stopped as soon as you find out you are pregnant

src.q: The hyperglycaemic effect of beta-blockers and diazoxide may be enhanced by thiazides.

rules.consequence: Thiazides may increase hypersensitivity reactions to allopurinol; uric acid may rise.
rules.action: Be aware; uricosuric doses may need adjusting.

src.q: Co-administration of thiazide may increase the incidence of hypersensitivity reactions of allopurinol.

rules.consequence: Reduced renal excretion of methotrexate and potentiated myelosuppression.
rules.action: Be aware of reduced methotrexate excretion and increased myelosuppression (no specific action stated in the SmPC).

src.q: Thiazides may reduce the renal excretion of cytotoxic medicinal products and potentiate their myelosuppressive effects.
Anticholinergic agents (e.g. atropine, biperiden) may increase the bioavailability of thiazide-type diuretics

rules.action: Be aware of the additive effect.

src.q: Telmisartan may increase the hypotensive effect of other antihypertensive agents.
